summary: File being tired of a ruler under sense 2
rationale: The example's 'ʕaǧizi m-u=ḥəkəm d-u=malk-ano' means being tired of this king's rule. The preceding Turoyo 24/236 mentions liberation 'mi zoriye, m taʕadda du malkano', and 24/237 says people will gladly accept the former king's son. This is discontent with something, explicitly covered by sense 2 'einer Sache überdrüssig werden', rather than physical fatigue or feeling unwell in sense 3. The edition likewise says 'der Herrschaft dieses Königs müde'.

summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 3 in Preterit (JTM 1.6/13)

data.turoyo: W ašər maškelan aʕlayye ste, w fayišina dəžmən, w bəṯr lə qadiri d saymi mede b aḥna i rastiye, yaʕni aš šaxṣat d maḥatlan bann awraqat w flan, ġalabe maʕǧəzilan, azzən lam maḥkamat ʕəloye ste, ṭayuṯo wa. Hənne naḥaq wayne, w duwenawo aḥna gməḥkəminawo ḥəkəm rabo, amma hənne lə ḥkimi.
data.translation: Wir erhoben Anklage gegen sie und wir wurden zu Feinden. Letztlich konnten sie wirklich nicht viel gegen uns ausrichten, die Personen, die wir in den Akten benannt hatten. Wir schikanierten sie sehr (indem wir sie anklagten) und sie gingen bis zu den höheren Gerichten. So war es bei den Muslimen: Sie waren im Unrecht, und wenn wir es gewesen wären, hätte man uns zu einer schweren Strafe verurteilt, doch sie wurden nicht verurteilt.

rationale: First III Preterit and first III.3 example; object and agents are recoverable from legal dispute, nonphysical harassment.

summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 3 in Preterit (113/179)

data.turoyo: Komər mḥela, axər ʕal u tarʕo həngi maʕəǧzila, komər nafiqo Zamrud, məlla: "Man yo hayo?"
data.translation: Sie klopfte wieder an die Tür, bis sie sie schließlich müde gemacht hatte. Zamrud trat heraus und sprach: Wer ist da?

rationale: Thin III.3 Preterit cell; persistent knocking causes annoyance; exact argument segmentation remains a question.

summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 4 in Preterit (65/491)

data.turoyo: "Ya Ḥasse", — omər, — "me raḥuqo koṯat. W maʕǧazlux u səsyawo! Baṭilat, izux, itaw taḥt u kon, arfi bəhən diḏux, hul d məṯnoḥat w bəṯr itux!"
data.translation: Ramazan sagte: "Ḥasse, du kommst von weit her und hast dies Pferd da müde geritten. Du bist müde; geh, setze dich unter das Zelt und verschnaufe dich, bis du dich ausgeruht hast, und dann komm!"

rationale: First example for new physical tiring sense III.4; named rider and overt horse object.

data.translation: <...> Often I am aware that I wearied him by going and coming to him. I ask his forgiveness. <...>

rationale: III.3 Preterit has two round-1 examples; repeated visits and apology support troubling, without forcing physical exhaustion in III.4. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

data.turoyo: Di walaye ʕaǧizi mene. Koṯe li walay, oxəl w nofəq. Kəzze lad darbe dan noše, kəmšalaḥḥe w qoṭelən. Hawi mal gabe ġalabe d lo ḥəzbe.
data.translation: wärend sie ihm gegenüber ganz machtlos waren. Darnach pflegte er in die Stadt zu kommen, um zu essen, und wieder hinauszugehen; auch auf die Strassen ging er, beraubte die Leute und brachte sie um, bis er sich masslose Reichtümer angeeignet hatte.

rationale: Thin I.1 Preterit Intransitive cell; explicit townspeople unable to resist an adversary.

data.turoyo: U abro di pire naqqa ḥreto mḥalaqle bəṯre. ʕAǧəz, u zʕurano mu abro di pire səmle, lo səmle, lo qadər maxlaṣ ruḥe mine.
data.translation: Da lief der Sohn der alten wieder hinter ihm her. Der Junge warmachtlos gegenüber dem Sohn der alten. Was er auch anstellte, er konnte ihn nicht loswerden.

rationale: Thin I.1 cell; both m-marked adversary and lo qadər maxlaṣ ruḥe independently support inability.

summary: example for sense 2 in Part act. (JTM 4.4/16)

data.turoyo: komər ax Malke, latno ʕaǧizo menux ġer mu dəmdəmano diḏux, latno ʕaǧizo mi xaraze w mu gurno, ġer mu dəmdəmano diḏux d ksaymət b qarʕi.
data.translation: Er sagte: Ach, Malke, ich bin deiner nicht überdrüssig, nur deines Gemurmels. Ich bin nicht die Einfassung und den Trog leid, nur dieses Gemurmel, mit dem du meinen Kopf bedröhnst.

rationale: First I.2 Part act. cell; negation and m-stimuli distinguish annoyance from bodily fatigue. One quotation contains both tokens.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit-wa (Lahdo Traitor 1/48)

data.turoyo: Ono qḥərwayno. Fayəš ġalabe ʕaǧəzwayno w omanno, mən d howe, gdomanno, mən d oṯe qəm femi, gdomanno, law... hič haw ksamno tə hno.
data.translation: I was annoyed! I was very distressed and said to myself: whatever happens I do not care and whatever comes to my mind I will say it without thinking of the consequences.

rationale: Thin I.2 Preterit-wa cell, independent English edition with explicit distressed first-person speaker.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit-wa (63/20)

data.turoyo: Ḥəngi d kətwa u ṭaʕnayḏi yaquro w baṭəlwayno taḥte, ʕaǧəzwayno me ruhi, ṭləbli u mawtayḏi mu alohayḏi.
data.translation: Weil meine Last so schwer war und ich darunter müde geworden und meiner selbst überdrüssig geworden war, bat ich Gott um meinen Tod.

rationale: Thin Preterit-wa sense 2; me ruhi as stimulus of dejection contrasts with separate fatigue baṭəlwayno.

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit Intransitive (66/43)

data.turoyo: Bəṯr me d hawən ʕaǧəz, li Səttiye əmmo: "Mammo!" Omər: "Mən yo ḥurma?" Əmmo: "Ašər, ʕaǧizina, gdəmxina! Elo hulan soz ʕam ḥḏoḏe, d bi saġityaḏan d saymina ḥḏoḏe.
data.translation: Als sie müde geworden waren, sagte Sittiye: "Mammo! Was ist, Frau?" "Wir sind müde geworden, wir wollen schlafen. Aber erst, wenn wir einander versprochen haben, daß wir, solange wir leben, nur einander nehmen wollen.

rationale: Thin I.3 Preterit Intransitive cell; overt sleep proposal supports physical tiredness, 1pl form.

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit Intransitive (91/21)

data.turoyo: Mi səbba d aḥna ʕaǧizina ġalabe mu talgo w mu kroxo, d mede lə zbəṭlan me ṣafro hul ʕaṣriye w mu baṭlo w mu kafno baṭilina w hənnək ste bu šəklawo ġalabe kafini w ġalabe ṣahən.
data.translation: Denn wir waren von dem Schnee, und weil wir vorn Morgen bis zum Abend herumgelaufen waren, ohne etwas zu erjagen, sehr ermattet, und von der Anstrengung und vom Hunger sehr müde geworden; jene aber waren auch sehr hungrig und durstig.

rationale: Thin I.3 cell; snow and prolonged wandering explicitly code bodily causes with m-. Cell now five after correcting 24/237.

data.translation: <...> I am not bothered except by his mumbling. <...> I am not bothered by taking him there and bringing him back, but by his mumbling on the road.

rationale: JTM 1.6/13 and 113/179 explicitly show causing distress through legal pressure or persistent knocking. Clarifies directed annoyance beyond the inherited German wording; no new participant frame.

summary: I has subject-coded experiencers, whereas III has L-suffix agents and affected objects. In III.2 ruḥayye is an overt reflexive object; neither German reflexive wording nor psychological meaning alone implies Detransitive morphology.

m- does not uniquely distinguish I.1/2/3: inability uses adversaries, aversion uses disliked persons or activities, and fatigue can name physical causes (91/21). b- explicitly marks hunting in MAC MuA Quzko/7 and the office in 33/55, while b gawe du baḥar and bi walaye can be locative.

I.2 and I.3 overlap lexically, but co-occurring anger, refusal or rejection supports aversion; journey, snow, sweating or sleep supports bodily fatigue. Retain inherited 63/131 under I.1 because failure to climb is explicit, though fatigue is also involved.

qaṭəl forms frequently denote a resulting current state; -wa places distress in background or prior time. Part act. predicates coexist with morphologically similar feminine qaṭəl forms, so source shape and agreement require attention.
PrS 44/40 can be inability or frustration; retain I.1 provisionally with no example. New III.4 gives a clear causative counterpart to physical fatigue, while harassment remains III.3.

Individual supplied occurrences are decided exactly once. The six repeated ʕaǧize tokens are grouped by the input into one record; its decision and selected example retain the repetition rather than inventing six extra records.
Round-1 example moves already change the I.1/2/3 counts and fill I.2 Preterit Intransitive to five. Jan 2.5/1206 therefore adds no needed example to that cell.
I experiencers are subject-coded; III maʕǧazli has a first-person agent and an unexpressed affected person recoverable from the visit context. Neither is Detransitive.
maʕǧəzono coordinates with ṭərpilo in a predicative hindrance description. Its shape and number do not securely establish ordinary Part act.; no new obstruction sense or new box is published.
Gədʕəǧaznowo signals an unreal fatigue result, but the supplied one-line exclamation lacks its antecedent; it is recorded without adding a context-poor example.
MAC NE Dilo and Falako/61: exhaustion or emotional distress? MAC NE Old woman and a fox/47: identify ʕAǧizono morphology and intended discomfort.
95/17: alignment flag notes a polarity mismatch in the final going-to-brother clause. Verify edition translation; none is quoted from this record.
65/491 and 113/179: confirm argument segmentation in maʕǧazlux and maʕəǧzila and whether the latter means annoyance or bodily exhaustion.
65/375: confirm ʕaǧizutu as Preterit Intransitive rather than a participial predicate; 65/489: verify printed ku šarrano without reconstructing a preposition.
Review the remaining I.1/2/3 boundary at PrS 44/40 and 63/131 without assigning senses from German müde alone.
Is maʕǧəzono (Jan 4.I/358) a lexical hindrance noun, a derived adjective, or an agreeing Part act. form? Exact/related form lookup does not resolve this. Verify before adding an obstruction sense.
In Jan 2.1/8 is the omitted affected person the priest, and does maʕǧazli mean bother or physical tiring? III.3 is preferred from the apology and repeated visits.
Supply the preceding condition for Gədʕəǧaznowo (Jan 4.I/555) before using it as a self-contained counterfactual example.
Does the weariness cluster Jan 1.46/2004 specifically express bodily fatigue or broader discouragement? I.3 is retained provisionally; the repetition alone does not separate the two.
Correct plural agreement: sollte to sollten
rationale: The subject 'die Leute' is plural, so the finite verb must be 'sollten'. This is a grammatical slip independent of any translation preference.
